CVE-2026-123142 [MCP]: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.4 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user holding an MCP-scoped OAuth token to perform unauthorized issuable state changes on issues and merge requests, including approving and merging, due to incorrect authorization checks.

CVE-2026-129875 [MCP]: REBUILD 4.5.0 through 4.5.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to recover the administrator password hash by filtering User.password through the MCP QueryRecords tool. Attackers can send LK2 prefix-match filters to the /gw/mcp/sse gateway and use the returned total count as an oracle to extract the SHA-256 hash one character at a time, then log in as administrator.

CVE-2026-126681 [MCP]: Improper restriction of intended endpoints in the connection configuration handling of the AWS Labs Timestream for InfluxDB MCP Server (awslabs.timestream-for-influxdb-mcp-server) before 0.0.19 might allow a remote unauthenticated actor (via prompt injection) to obtain the InfluxDB API token configured on the server, sent to a crafted endpoint controlled through an InfluxDB URL introduced in the MCP client context. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.0.19 or later and rotate any InfluxDB API tokens configured for the server.

CVE-2026-68934 [MCP]: code-review-mcp-server automates code review and can post comments directly on GitHub pull requests. Prior to 1.5.3, the getLocalGitDiff, codeReview, createPR, and getPRTemplate MCP tools accept caller-controlled folderPath and baseBranch string parameters that are interpolated into command strings executed by child_process.execSync through /bin/sh. Shell metacharacters, command substitution, or quote-breaking input can therefore execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the host process running the MCP server. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.3.
